standard_prerequisites.name: Mere relation and reflexivity
standard_prerequisites.statement: A mere relation R on X is a family of mere propositions, and it is reflexive when \prd{x:X} R(x,x) is inhabited.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis on the relation (source lines 265-267).

standard_prerequisites.name: A relation implying identity
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the map whose continuity the first proof exploits and whose total-space behaviour the second proof studies.

standard_prerequisites.name: Axiom K and being a set
standard_prerequisites.statement: X is a set exactly when Axiom K holds, i.e. every loop p : \id[X]xx equals \refl x.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what the first proof establishes (source lines 291-293).

standard_prerequisites.name: Contracibility of the total space of paths
standard_prerequisites.statement: For fixed x the type \sm{y:X} \id[X]xy is contractible, with centre (x,\refl x).
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the second proof to contractibility of the total space of R (source lines 296-303).

core_obligations: Observe that the two assertions of the theorem are equivalent, so that either one may be proved (source lines 273-278).

First proof: for a loop p : \id[X]xx apply the dependent action on paths of f(x) at p and rewrite the resulting dependent path through the arrow-type rule to get \trans{p}{f(x,x,r)} = f(x,x,\trans{p}r) (source lines 283-288).

Substitute r \defeq \rho(x) and use that both \trans{p}r and r lie in the mere proposition R(x,x), so that the equation becomes f(x,x,\rho(x)) \ct p = f(x,x,\rho(x)), and cancel to get p = \refl x, hence Axiom K (source lines 289-293).

Second proof: show each f(x,y) is an equivalence by showing f induces an equivalence of total spaces, whose target is contractible by thm:contr-paths, and prove the source contractible with centre (x,\rho(x)) (source lines 295-303).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to either direction by showing the two assertions equivalent.
First proof: make f continuous in its arguments and cancel to obtain Axiom K.
Second proof: compare the total spaces and compute the centre of contraction.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled theorem at source lines 265-269 (book Theorem 7.2.2): if R is a reflexive mere relation on X that implies identity, then X is a set and R(x,y) is equivalent to \id[X]{x}{y}. The statement contains no proof idea, and the author gives two different proofs. The first has to use the continuity of the map f : \prd{x,y} R(x,y) \to (\id[X]xy): it applies the dependent action on paths of f(x) to a loop p, rewrites the resulting dependent path by the arrow-type rule into a transport equation, collapses one side using that R(x,x) is a mere proposition, and finally cancels to obtain p = \refl x and hence Axiom K. The second works instead with total spaces: it shows f induces an equivalence of \sm{y:X}R(x,y) with \sm{y:X}\id[X]xy, which is contractible, and proves the first total space contractible with centre (x,\rho(x)) by reducing the required equality through the path type of a \Sigma-type and the mere-proposition hypothesis on R. Neither argument is determined by the statement, and each uses a different mechanism.
